title: feat(storage,mcp): one upload link takes several files on a multi-file field
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_

Fixes #32747

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here — the served MCP skill (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`, the `create_upload_link` lines) and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` say a multi-file field's link takes up to 10 files and explain `count`; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 47f names the reserved ids. No file under `skills/**` teaches upload links (`git grep -i "upload.link\|create_upload_link" -- skills/` finds nothing). The Console's skill download (`objectstack-skill.ts`) renders the no-scope skill, which carries no file tools, so its byte-identical mirror needs no change and its drift pin stays green.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：多文件字段（`multiple: true`）的上传链接，一次可以选并提交多个文件（最多 10 个），每个文件各得一个文件 id；单文件字段和附件链接仍然只收一个文件。
- **为什么改**：用户说"这是我的三张发票"时，以前要开三个链接、传三次；现在一个链接、一次选择就够了（裁决 A）。
- **风险与回滚**：一次提交全部成功或全部不留：任一文件超限或字段不接受，整批拒绝、链接不被消耗；落盘或写记录失败，整批文件都被清掉，记录保持原样。回滚就是还原这个 PR，现有单文件链接的行为和拒绝码不变（成功应答只多了 `fileIds`）。
- **先看**：`record-file-access.ts` 的 `consumeUploadLinkFiles`（检查顺序、一次消耗、失败清理），以及记录尚未创建时 `count` 预留 id 的那一段。
- **两分钟验证**：跑 `record-file-access.integration.test.ts` 里 `#32747` 那一组（19 个用例），和 dogfood 的 `showcase-mcp-record-files`（一个链接、三张 PDF）。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

<details><summary>The storage door: one submit, several files, all or nothing</summary>

- `consumeUploadLinkFiles(token, uploads[], caller)` is the one path; `consumeUploadLink` wraps it with a one-element array, so a one-file send takes the same steps in the same order as before, except on a multi-file field's record link, where the field's `accept` / `maxSize` is now judged before the spend (see Acceptance notes).
- How many files a submit takes (`fileRangeOf`):
  - an attachments link: 1;
  - a record's field link: up to `UPLOAD_LINK_MAX_FILES` (10) when the field declares `multiple: true`, else 1;
  - a link for a record not yet created: exactly its `count`.
  The spec has no max-items key for a file field, so the cap is the platform constant. A wrong count is refused `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR` through `sendError` before the link is spent, and says how many the link takes.
- Before the spend, every file is judged on the workspace's upload size limit (`413`), and, on a link that takes several (a multi-file field's, or a link for a record not yet created), on the field's own `accept` / `maxSize`, however many files the send carries. A refusal stores nothing and leaves the link usable. A link that takes one file is judged as before (to a record, the record's write judges the field's constraints).
- After the spend, the files are stored and committed one by one, then the record's field gains them all in **one** write (`[...current, ...ids]`). Any store failing, or that write refusing (a pending approval's lock, say), discards every file of the send, rows and bytes, so the record shows what it held before.
- A link for a record not yet created takes `count` (1–10, more than 1 only on a `multiple: true` field). The mint reserves the extra ids as `pending` rows named `upload-link (reserved)`, owned by the minting user, and answers `fileIds: [link id, ...reserved]`. The upload fills each id with the same `pre_record_upload` binding a single upload's id gets (that user, that object and field, one record, one hour). A failed mint takes the link and every reserved row back. A link whose stored reserved ids repeat one, or name the link's own id, is the one unusable link.
- The `PUT /upload-links/:token` door reads a several-file send as one `multipart/form-data` form carrying `count` and `file0` … `fileN-1` (indexed names, since a form parser that keeps one value per name keeps only the last of a repeated one), marked by the header `x-upload-link-form: several`, which the page sends with it.
  - The door reads a body as that form only when it is `multipart/form-data`, carries the header, and the link takes several files: for such a body it reads the link first (a read that writes nothing), and the form declares at most as many files as that link takes, each within the upload limit, plus 64 KiB of framing.
  - Any other body, on any link, is the file itself, whatever its content type, under the one-file limit, with the same checks in the same order as on `main`: a multipart body without the header (on a multi-file field's link too), and the page's form sent to a link that takes one file (a single-file field's, an attachments link, a `count: 1` link). So does a marked form to a link the door cannot read: its spend answers the refusal it answered on `main`, in `main`'s order.
  - A `count` over what the link takes is refused `400` `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and a form whose parts disagree with `count` (or misses a part) `400` `INVALID_REQUEST`, both before any part's bytes are read.
  - Every success answer now also carries `fileIds`.
- When a store throws after the spend, its key is deleted with the rest of the send, as a single upload's is.
- Also touched to carry the new member: `file-attachment-service.ts` (pass-through), `storage-service-plugin.ts` (the door resolver requires it), `upload-link-wire.ts` (the cap, its code and status, the form's field names).

</details>

<details><summary>The page, the MCP tool, docs</summary>

- `upload-link-page.ts`: `<input type="file" multiple>` where the link takes several; the script checks the pick count and sends the form. New sentences in `upload-link-copy.ts` for every locale it serves (pick up to N; pick exactly N; N files attached / received; wrong count).
- `create_upload_link` (MCP): the description says a multi-file field's link takes up to 10 files, sent together, and that one refused file refuses the send. Optional `count` (1 to 10 in the schema) is offered where links for a record not yet created are; `count` with a `recordId` is refused before the bridge is asked. No new tool.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`: the bridge member's target type takes `count`.
- Docs: `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 47f. Changeset: `.changeset/32747-upload-link-multiple-files.md` (patch: service-storage, mcp, runtime).

</details>

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins and what each refuses</summary>

`packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.integration.test.ts`, describe `#32747 — one link, several files` (19 cases), on a fixture field `claim.scans` (`multiple: true`, PDF only):

- a record link takes 3 PDFs: three ids, the field holds all three;
- a link for a record not yet created, `count: 3`: three ids, one submit fills them, the create takes all three;
- before the upload, a reserved id is refused to every write (the uploader's own, a reviewer, system), the download door answers `404`, and it is not a link;
- the cap: 11 files `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before the spend, then 10 land;
- exact count: 2 of 3 refused before the spend, then 3 land;
- CONTROL: for a single-file field link and an attachments link, the spend refuses two files (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, "takes one file"; the door never reads a form for them), then the one lands, then the link is gone (`404`); and the mint refuses `count` of 0, 11 or 1.5, and above 1 on a single-file field (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`);
- another signed-in user gets the one unusable-link `404` and spends nothing;
- file 2 of 3 the field does not take: the whole send is refused before the spend (`ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT`), the record unchanged, the link usable;
- file 2 of 3 failing in the storage write after the spend: `500`, the record unchanged, no row and no bytes of the send left, and the key whose upload threw deleted too (a record link and a pre-record link);
- the record's write refusing after the spend (a lock): `409`, the record unchanged, none of the files kept;
- a form that lost a part: `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, nothing spent;
- a multi-file field's record link and one PNG (as a form, and as the request body): `400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` before the spend, nothing stored, the link then takes a PDF;
- a single-file field link and an attachments link take a `multipart/form-data` body as the file, as on `main`: declared 1 MiB + 1 under a 1 MiB limit is `413` with `main`'s words (a form's allowance would have taken it), and the body is stored with its own length as the size;
- a single-file field link and an attachments link take the page's own marked form as the file too: declared 1 MiB + 1 is `413` with the same words;
- a multipart body without the header, even one shaped like the form, is the file on a multi-file field's record link and on a `count: 1` link: `413` with `main`'s words over the one-file limit, else `200` with the body's length as the size;
- the page's form to a used link, declared over the one-file limit: `413` with `main`'s words, then `404`;
- a link whose stored reserved ids name a file twice, or the link's own id: the one unusable-link `404`, nothing stored;
- a form declaring 2 MiB under a 1 MiB limit is accepted on a multi-file field link;
- a form refused before any part is read: `count` 11 and `count` 999 (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR`), parts fewer than `count` and a missing `file1` (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`), each with zero reads; a good form reads each part once;
- the page: `multiple` on a multi-file link, the exact-count sentence on a `count` link, no `multiple` on a single-file link, and its form sent with `x-upload-link-form: several`.

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`, describe `[#32747] create_upload_link: one link, several files` (5 cases): `count` passes to the bridge and the answer names every id; no `count` asks the bridge as before; `count` with a `recordId` is refused before the bridge; `count` is offered only where a link can name no record, and the description says a multi-file link takes several; the served skill teaches both.

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts`, describe `[#32747] one link, three PDFs (dogfood_upload_claim.invoices)` (3 cases, a real `FormData` through the served stack): a claim link takes three PDFs and `read_file` reads each; `count: 3` and `create_record` takes the three ids; one PDF of three over the size limit refuses the send (`413`, nothing stored), then the same link takes the three.

Two existing expectations in the integration file now include the additive `fileIds`; one dogfood expectation for #32686 does too.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations: each new negative pin, with the forbidden behaviour put back</summary>

Each through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor must hit, the mutation is verified on disk, the file is restored to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty after each):

| Mutation | Red |
| --- | --- |
| drop the file-count check before the spend | cap, exact count, CONTROL (3 failed) |
| judge `accept` / `maxSize` before the spend only for a pre-record link | file 2 of 3 the field does not take (1 failed) |
| pre-record failure discards only the last id | storage write fails on file 2 (1 failed) |
| record failure discards only the last file | storage write fails on file 2; the lock after the spend (2 failed) |
| reserved rows stored `committed` instead of `pending` | the reserved-id refusals and 3 more (4 failed) |
| drop the link's same-user check | the stranger pins, old and new (2 failed) |
| a single-file field link takes up to 10 | CONTROL, the page pins (6 failed) |
| mint `count` above 1 on a single-file field | CONTROL (1 failed) |
| mint `count` above 10 | CONTROL (1 failed) |
| a form's part count and missing-part checks off | the lost-part pin (1 failed) |
| MCP: `count` with a `recordId` passed to the bridge | that MCP pin (1 failed) |
| (round 1) a multi-file record link's one-file send judged after the spend | the one-PNG pin (1 failed) |
| (round 2) every link reads a form, a one-file link included | the one-file multipart pin (1 failed: `400 INVALID_REQUEST` instead of `413`) |
| (round 3) any multipart body read as the form, no header needed | the unmarked-multipart pin (1 failed) |
| (round 3) a link the door cannot read refused at the inspect | the used-link `413` pin (1 failed: `404` before `413`) |
| (round 3) reserved ids not checked for repeats or the link's own id | the forged-reserved-ids pin (1 failed) |
| (round 1) `count` over the link's cap not refused in the door | the zero-reads pin (1 failed) |
| (round 1) each part read while the form is still being checked | the zero-reads pin (1 failed) |
| (round 1) a key whose upload threw left in place, pre-record and record | the storage-write pin (1 failed each) |
| (round 1) MCP `count` without `.max(10)` | the MCP schema pin (1 failed) |
| size limit judged on the first file only (rebuilt `dist`, dogfood) | one PDF of three over the limit (1 failed: `200`, three files stored) |

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Condition 1, no narrowing of existing links.** Every body `main` took as the file is still the file, on every link, except a `multipart/form-data` body carrying `x-upload-link-form: several` (a header `main` never defined) sent to a link that takes several files, which is read as the form. Every other body takes the same path, checks, limit and order as on `main`, with the same codes and statuses. The one answer change is additive: every success answer also carries `fileIds`.
- **The one judgement that moved (accepted as the cost of F1).** A one-file send through a multi-file field's record link is now judged on the field's `accept` / `maxSize` before the spend, with the same code and status the record's write answered (`400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT`), and the link stays usable instead of spent.
- **Condition 2, a reserved id before its upload.** The uploader's own write naming it is refused by the incomplete-upload arm (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `invalid_value`, "its upload was never completed"); any other user's or a system write by the pre-record arm (`not_yours`, the unreadable-file words), since the reserved row is recognised as a link's row. The download door answers `404 FILE_NOT_FOUND` (a `pending` file is not served), `read_file` reads only files a record holds, and the row is `pending`, so `sys_file`'s retention (`status: 'pending'`, 7 days) reaps it if the link is never used. The link's own id keeps its existing refusals.
- **Condition 3, partial failure after the spend.** Pinned by failing file 2 of 3 in the storage write: the record is unchanged and no `sys_file` row or stored bytes of the send are left, for a record link and a pre-record link. A record write refusing after the spend (a lock) is pinned the same way.
- Attachments links stay one file (the seat's Q2); a link for a record not yet created takes exactly `count` (Q1).
- The Console skill mirror is unchanged: it renders the skill a no-scope caller gets, which has no file tools, and its byte-identical test is green.
- Other places that say "one file" about links (`mcp-http-tools.ts`, `storage-routes.ts`, `upload-link-copy.ts`, `pre-record-upload.ts`, `skill-md.ts`) were read; the ones describing a link's use are updated, the rest describe a single upload or file and stay.
